correctness.rationale: The normalized polar integrals yield diagonal entries a(1-e^{-t}), a(1-(1+t)e^{-t}) and mixed entry G(t) Z_E/(2π), where G is the lower incomplete gamma. The circle rearrangement |Z_E|≤2sin(πa) has unique arc equality. Exact traceless Hermitian matrix multiplication gives squared commutator norm four times a cross-product quadratic; maximizing its strictly concave dependence on cosδ gives both branches and all equality masks. The quotient ρ_a(t) has a strictly decreasing positive integral representation from infinity to zero, proving a unique transition. The packaged symbolic checker verified the exact algebra, with 1,353 additional finite/numerical checks of integrals, critical radii and masks. Finite tests are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The objective is a natural incompatibility measure for two finite-aperture Gaussian Fock concentration measurements. For every pair of angular coverages it solves an infinite-dimensional measurable mask-design optimization exactly, classifies all optimal shapes as arcs, and identifies a unique nontrivial radial transition between antipodal and non-antipodal orientation geometry. The phase boundary cannot be read from a single-operator norm or a generic matrix norm without establishing and optimizing the attainable Gaussian apertures. The theorem is specifically scoped to the two-mode model; no downstream full-Fock theorem is asserted.
